'''March Tian Boedihardjo''' ({{zh|t={{linktext|沈|詩|鈞}}}}) is a Hong Kong mathematician. He is a former [[child prodigy]] of ethnic [[Hoklo people|Hokkien]] descent with ancestry from [[Anxi County|Anxi]], [[Quanzhou]], [[China]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://hk.lifestyle.appledaily.com/nextplus/magazine/article/20070830/2_10085009/|title=億 萬 家 財 蒸 發 9 歲 神 童 身 世 傳 奇| date=30 August 2007}}</ref> As of 2023, he is an assistant professor of mathematics at [[Michigan State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Personal Homepage of March Boedihardjo |url=https://apps.math.msu.edu/PageSpace/pb/boedihardjo |access-date=2024-03-15 |website=apps.math.msu.edu}}</ref>

==Biography==
Boedihardjo was born to an ethnic Chinese family in Hong Kong, with family roots in [[Anxi County|Anxi]], China.{{citation needed|date=September 2019}} Boedihardjo moved to the [[United Kingdom]] in 2005, when his older brother Horatio began studying at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="Telegraph"/>

Boedihardjo finished his [[Advanced Level (UK)|A-level exam]]s in Britain at the age of nine years and three months, after attending [[Greene's Tutorial College|Greene's College Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=9-year-old maths whiz-kid wins university place |url=https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/9-year-old-maths-whiz-kid-wins-university-place-1.196907 |access-date=2022-08-18 |website=gulfnews.com |date=26 August 2007 |language=en}}</ref><ref group=note>Record for the youngest person to pass maths A-level with an A grade at the time, but has since been surpassed by [[Yasha Asley]], see {{Cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/hampshire/7941327.stm |title=Boy, 8, sets A-level maths record  |work=BBC News |date=13 March 2009}} and {{Cite news|date=2011-03-30|title=Boy, 8, gets A in A-level maths|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leicestershire-12852989|access-date=2020-05-16}}</ref> He also gained 8 [[GCSE]]s.<ref name="Telegraph">{{cite news|last=Spencer |first=Richard |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/main.jhtml?xml=/news/2007/08/25/nalevel225.xml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070907073354/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/main.jhtml?xml=/news/2007/08/25/nalevel225.xml |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 September 2007 |title=Maths boy, 9, wins university place |publisher=Daily Telegraph |date=25 August 2007 |accessdate=16 March 2011}}</ref> He was accepted at [[Hong Kong Baptist University]], making him the youngest ever university student in Hong Kong. He commenced his university studies in September 2007.<ref name=bbc>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/6961865.stm |title=BBC NEWS, Child star wins university place |publisher=BBC News |date=24 August 2007 |access-date=16 March 2011}}</ref> The university tailored a special 5-year curriculum programme for Boedihardjo which he criticized as being too easy and unstimulating on the first day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2007-09/06/content_6669615.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080221233322/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2007-09/06/content_6669615.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 February 2008 |title=University 'very easy' for Hong Kong nine-year-old boy |publisher=Xinhua |date=6 September 2007 |accessdate=16 March 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/article/606720/i-know-it-all-already-says-junior-genius-his-historic-first-day-university |title=I know it all already, says junior genius on his historic first day of university |publisher=South China Morning Post |date=5 September 2007 |accessdate=28 September 2012}}</ref> He obtained A−'s and B+'s in most of his mathematics courses in his first year, which got him on the Dean's List.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www1.appledaily.atnext.com/template/apple/art_main.cfm?iss_id=20080708&sec_id=4104&subsec_id=11866&art_id=11323085 |title=Archived copy |website=www1.appledaily.atnext.com |access-date=13 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080710062057/http://www1.appledaily.atnext.com/template/apple/art_main.cfm?iss_id=20080708&sec_id=4104&subsec_id=11866&art_id=11323085 |archive-date=10 July 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He was conferred a [[Bachelor of Science]] in Mathematical Science and a [[Master of Philosophy]] in Mathematics after completing his programme one year early in 2011.<ref>[http://tvscripts.edt.reuters.com/2007-08-23/ea311d8.html Tvscripts.edt.reuters, Hong Kong Prodigy]{{dead link|date=July 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://net2.hkbu.edu.hk/~enews/view_article.php?id=118 |title=HKBU admits nine-year-old applicant March Tian Boedihardjo |publisher=HKBU |date=23 August 2007 |accessdate=16 March 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721085951/http://net2.hkbu.edu.hk/~enews/view_article.php?id=118 |archive-date=21 July 2011 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="Standard">{{cite web|url=http://www.thestandard.com.hk/news_detail.asp?we_cat=21&art_id=114051&sid=33353499&con_type=1&d_str=20110811&fc=7 |title=Maths genius counts days before leaving |publisher=The Standard |date=11 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019044222/http://www.thestandard.com.hk/news_detail.asp?we_cat=21&art_id=114051&sid=33353499&con_type=1&d_str=20110811&fc=7 |archivedate=19 October 2012 }}</ref><ref name = "HKBU">{{cite web |url=http://www.sci.hkbu.edu.hk/news/news_98.html |title=March Boedihardjo completes his double degrees at HKBU and will continue his research in Mathematics in the United States |publisher=HKBU |date=12 August 2011 |accessdate=29 November 2011 |archive-date=25 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425121616/http://www.sci.hkbu.edu.hk/news/news_98.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After graduating from Hong Kong Baptist University, Boedihardjo studied at [[Texas A&M University]] as a visiting scholar and then as a PhD student.<ref name="HKBU" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/article/975993/double-degree-adds-hk-maths-prodigy |title=Double degree adds up for HK maths prodigy |publisher=South China Morning Post |date=13 August 2011 |accessdate=28 September 2012}}</ref> In 2017, Boediharjo took up the position of [[Adjunct professors in the United States|assistant adjunct professor]] at [[UCLA]] on a three-year contract,<ref>{{Cite web|last=黃樂怡|date=2017-01-12|title=【神童再創神話】9歲讀大學 18歲沈詩鈞在美國UCLA做教授|url=https://www.hk01.com/熱爆話題/65293/神童再創神話-9歲讀大學-18歲沈詩鈞在美國ucla做教授|access-date=2020-10-11|website=香港01|language=zh-HK}}</ref> a position he held until 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/people/visiting/march|title=Visiting Faculty|publisher=UCLA Department of Mathematics|accessdate=16 May 2020}}</ref> He was a visiting assistant professor at [[UC Irvine]] from 2021 to 2022 before starting a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoc]] at ETH Zurich, a position he held until 2023. He is currently an assistant professor of mathematics at Michigan State University.
